summary.intent: Work through a list of review findings on release-related PRs in the callisto repo: update the PR text for the npm publish-confirmation fix (#435), then resolve the #431 (release PR hold note) conflicts and code/test findings.
summary.outcome: Updated #435's title and body, rebased the #431 branch onto origin/main (resolving a REL-PR-09 conflict in docs/specs/release.json), and implemented the #431 fixes: no duplicate note on lookup failure, a failure-note job in the release workflow, and new tests. The final step (merging the rebased result as a fast-forward-safe merge commit via target/merge-hold-note.sh) was run but its result is not shown in the transcript.

repo: Force pushes are disallowed by repo rules, so a rebased branch is landed as a merge commit on top of the existing remote branch, which keeps it a plain fast-forward push.

The release workflow policy test (.github/tests/verify-release-workflow-policy.sh) allowlists which jobs may hold PR write scopes, so any new job that writes to PRs must be added to that allowlist deliberately.

Release CI checks live in .github/tests: verify-release-workflow-policy.sh, verify-release-workflow-contract.sh and verify-action-pins.sh. Workflows are also linted with actionlint and zizmor, and scripts with shellcheck.
note-release-pr-rebuild.sh takes an outcome of success|failure|skipped, and now fails on any outcome it doesn't know.
The release PR note test stub should serve real comment JSON and apply the script's own jq filter so marker lookup is actually exercised, with a failing-lookup mode.
docs/specs/release.json holds spec entries such as REL-PR-09, which both main and the feature branch changed, causing the rebase conflict.

The npm publish confirmation (`npm view`) must receive the same temporary config as the publish child, via `--userconfig` when CALLISTO_PUBLISH_NPM_CONFIG is set. Without it, restricted scoped packages return 404 and the check fails with E157. Cargo is unaffected.

code.finding: Changed so that a failed comment lookup no longer leads to creating a duplicate note comment.
The 'Say how the release PR rebuild ended' step moved into a job that runs even when verify or candidate selection fails, so a failure note is always posted.

workflow: Scratch helper scripts (resolve-spec.py, merge-hold-note.sh) are written to target/ and run with `python3 -I` for conflict resolution and scripted git operations.
Validate JSON after a scripted conflict resolution and grep for leftover conflict markers before running `git rebase --continue`.
Run the full local gate (policy, contract, pin checks, actionlint, zizmor, shellcheck) after workflow edits to catch allowlist violations early.

friction: The no-force-push rule meant the rebased #431 branch could not be pushed directly, forcing a merge-commit workaround.
The rebase hit a conflict in docs/specs/release.json (REL-PR-09) that needed a scripted resolution.
The new workflow job tripped the release-workflow policy check, which needed an allowlist edit.
actionlint output was noisy and needed grep filtering to see real issues.
The npm restricted-package behavior could not be verified for real without a private-scope registry.
open_items: Confirm the result of target/merge-hold-note.sh (merge commit and push of the #431 branch), as its output was not shown.
The real npm behavior against a restricted package is unverified for #435.
Remaining items on the user's list after #435 and #431 are not covered in this transcript.
docs/releasing.md was grepped for the release-pr-note reference, with no visible follow-up on whether docs need updating for the new failure-note job.
